extracted.intended_audience: agency officials, administrative law attorneys, regulators, and administrative adjudicators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on applying Section 5 of the Administrative Procedure Act: what notice must contain, opportunities for informal settlement, separation of functions in adjudications, and authority to issue declaratory orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — inspector/technical-testing determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal proceedings are not desired or utilized where immediate technical judgments by skilled inspectors or examiners are required (e.g., grading grain, testing radio equipment), because formal hearing gives no added protection and immediate decisions are necessary to protect the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resort to formal procedure is possible but not required; the inspector's judgment remains the determining element. Formal hearings do not necessarily give greater assurance of a correct decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — military, naval, or foreign affairs functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The section 'exempts military, naval, and foreign affairs functions' because such functions are for the same reasons exempted from section 1 and rarely, if ever, are statutes interpreted to require such functions to be exercised upon hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply exemption to exercises of adjudicatory functions to the extent military or naval or foreign affairs conduct is involved. Legislative history treats 'foreign affairs functions' consistently with section 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — agency acting as agent for a court
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Cases in which an agency is acting as an agent for a court' are exempt from the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-explanatory: when agency acts as court agent, the section's hearing rules do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — certification of employee representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemption for 'the certification of employee representatives such as the Labor Board operations under section 9(c) of the National Labor Relations Act' because such determinations rest largely upon an election or availability of an election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also exempts certification by the National Mediation Board under the Railway Labor Act; treat such certification determinations as outside section 5's hearing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice — timely information of time, place, and nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons entitled to notice of an agency hearing shall be timely informed of 'the time, place, and nature thereof.' 'Timely' depends on circumstances including urgency and complexity; nothing in subsection revokes specific statutory notice periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice should specify time and place and the nature of the hearing (e.g., whether a cease and desist order should issue). Consider statutory notice requirements (e.g., FTC 30 days) and the urgency/complexity of the matter when determining what is 'timely.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice — due regard for convenience and necessity of parties
rubrics_metrics.description: In fixing times and places for hearings, 'due regard shall be had for the convenience and necessity of the parties or their representatives.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should schedule hearings consistent with public interest and agency functions to be convenient for parties and their representatives where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice — legal authority and jurisdiction must be stated
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice should contain reference to the 'legal authority and jurisdiction under which the hearing is to be held' to inform parties of the powers and jurisdiction invoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient citation/description of authority so parties can raise relevant legal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice — matters of fact and law asserted
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must advise parties of 'the matters of fact and law asserted' but is not required to set forth evidentiary facts or legal argument; it need only indicate the legal and factual issues involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give enough specificity to inform parties what issues they need to meet without requiring full evidentiary detail or argument in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsive pleading requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where private persons are the moving parties, 'other parties to the proceeding shall give prompt notice of issues controverted in fact or law;' in other instances agencies may by rule require responsive pleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is mandatory when private parties move; agencies should require additional parties (e.g., competitors intervening in license applications) to disclose positions promptly; agencies may by rule require responsive pleadings when the agency is the moving party. Agencies may adopt rules prescribing consequences (e.g., deemed admissions) for failure to plead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for informal settlement or adjustment (section 5(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall afford interested parties opportunity for (1) 'the submission and consideration of facts, arguments, offers of settlement, or proposals of adjustment where time, the nature of the proceeding, and the public interest permit,' and (2) if parties cannot determine controversy by consent, hearing and decision upon notice and in conformity with sections 7 and 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opportunities may be provided before or after formal proceedings are initiated. Agencies may use oral conferences or require written proposals. If proposals are unsatisfactory, the agency should consider informing parties of conditions on which it will settle. Agencies may require consent decrees, stipulations, or orders as part of settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on informal settlement opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to provide informal settlement opportunities is limited to cases 'where time, the nature of the proceeding, and the public interest permit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency actions or proceedings with statutory time limits may justify limiting or refusing settlement opportunities. If informal settlement would not ensure future compliance or would not be in the public interest, agency may refuse settlement. Agencies should not defer formal proceedings indefinitely while parties delay by serial proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of agency procedures for informal settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency should make public, pursuant to section 3(a), the manner in which it will provide interested parties an opportunity for informal settlement or adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may publish procedures advising how informal settlements may be sought; where settlement opportunity is offered after issuance of notice/complaint, published procedures suffice to advise parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions — hearing officers prepare initial/recommended decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The officer who presides at reception of evidence pursuant to section 7 'shall make the recommended decision or initial decision required by section 8' except where such officers become unavailable to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the presiding officer becomes unavailable, the agency may complete the hearing itself or substitute another hearing officer to prepare the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions — prohibition on off-record consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for disposition of ex parte matters authorized by law, 'no such officer shall consult any person or party on any fact in issue unless upon notice and opportunity for all parties to participate;' hearing officers also must not be responsible to or subject to supervision or direction of investigative or prosecuting personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing officers may not obtain or receive evidentiary or factual information outside the record unless all parties are given notice and opportunity to participate; applies equally to expert testimony obtained informally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions — restriction on investigative/prosecuting personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: 'No officer, employee, or agent engaged in the performance of investigative or prosecuting functions for any agency in any case shall, in that or a factually related case, participate or advise in the decision, recommended decision, or agency review pursuant to section 8 except as witness or counsel in public proceedings.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff who investigated or prosecuted the case (or a factually related case) must present their views in public proceedings (hearings, oral argument, briefs) rather than by private consultation; this preserves the independence of decision-makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning and scope of 'factually related case'
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'factually related case' covers situations where a party faces two proceedings arising out of the same or a connected set of facts; investigative/prosecuting personnel who served in one such proceeding are precluded from assisting in decision of the related proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not broadly bar officials from assisting other cases merely because facts form a similar pattern; apply literal reading to related factual connections (e.g., same underlying investigation yields multiple proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted consultation with non-investigative agency personnel and staff organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearing officers may obtain advice from agency personnel not engaged in investigative or prosecuting functions (e.g., agency head, supervisors of hearing officers, staff assisting analysis). Agencies are encouraged to organize staff so advisers are free of investigative/prosecuting functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizing staff to separate investigative/prosecuting functions from advisers has advantages: makes principal advisers regularly available and allows publication of staff roles in agency rules to demonstrate compliance with section 5(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational placement of hearing examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: To satisfy separation of functions, hearing examiners should be placed in an organizational unit apart from investigative and prosecuting personnel and supervised only by agency officers who perform no investigative or prosecuting functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the general counsel supervises prosecution, the examiners' unit should not be under that supervision unless the supervising official has no responsibility for investigative/prosecuting functions; publish organizational rules to show compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from separation of functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 5(c) 'shall not apply in determining applications for initial licenses' and 'shall not apply in determining...the validity or application of rates, facilities, or practices of public utilities or carriers.' Also, it is 'not applicable in any manner to the agency or any member or members of the body comprising the agency.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret 'initial license' broadly to include original licenses and applications by licensees for modification; renewals, revocations, suspensions, and agency-initiated modifications remain subject to separation rules. The agency-as-body exemption recognizes that members who both investigate and decide are not excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for disposition of ex parte matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The exemption for 'the disposition of ex parte matters as authorized by law' permits hearing examiners to act without notice on matters such as requests for adjournments, continuances, filing of papers, and subpoenas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited, narrow category; does not undermine general prohibition on off-record consultations about facts in issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency review — restriction on consulting investigators/prosecutors
rubrics_metrics.description: On agency review, agency heads are precluded from consulting or obtaining advice from any officer or employee who investigated or prosecuted the case (or a factually related case); views of such officials must be presented in public proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages presentation of investigative/prosecutorial views through public channels (testimony, briefs, exceptions) rather than private advice in the decisional process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory orders authority (section 5(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency is authorized 'in its sound discretion, with like effect as in the case of other orders, to issue a declaratory order to terminate a controversy or remove uncertainty.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to develop predictability by authorizing binding determinations that dispose of legal controversies without requiring parties to act at their own risk; treat declaratory orders like other orders in effect.
